title: Multi-Cloud DNS Resolution Health

controlTest.positiveScenario: Replay sample `dns:health` events with `( OR sourcetype="synthetic:dns")` into `index=cloud`. Confirm UC-4.4.23 returns >=1 row and the alert fires.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Replay benign `dns:health` traffic without `( OR sourcetype="synthetic:dns")`. Confirm UC-4.4.23 returns zero rows and the alert does not fire.

dataSources: `index=cloud` sourcetype=`dns:health` collected via Custom (synthetic probes, Route 53 Resolver / Azure DNS / Cloud DNS logs); validate ingest with `| stats count by sourcetype`.
app: Custom (synthetic probes, Route 53 Resolver / Azure DNS / Cloud DNS logs)

description: UC-4.4.23 — Multi-Cloud DNS Resolution Health: queries Microsoft Azure `dns:health` for search criteria `( OR sourcetype="synthetic:dns")` and returns actor, resource, and region context for security review and change validation.
value: On Microsoft Azure, detecting 'Multi-Cloud DNS Resolution Health' early shortens cloud incident response and produces defensible audit evidence for identity and change-management controls. UC-4.4.23 drives high-priority security alerting before customer-impacting drift.
implementation: Emit probe results from each cloud (success, latency_ms, NXDOMAIN rate) via HEC. Optionally join Route 53 Resolver query logs for SERVFAIL spikes. Page when any critical FQDN fails from two vantage points or latency doubles vs baseline.
visualization: Status grid (FQDN × provider), Line chart (success rate over time), Single value (failed probes).
knownFalsePositives: This pattern can surge during change windows, in sandboxes, and when a platform is in maintenance, so we line alerts up with the calendar and take a second look before we call it an incident.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Splunk Enterprise or Splunk Cloud with search access to `index=cloud`.
• Install and configure Custom (synthetic probes, Route 53 Resolver / Azure DNS / Cloud DNS logs) with the modular input for `dns:health`.
• Prerequisite crawl UC(s): UC-4.4.33.
• Confirm field extractions in `props.conf` for `userIdentity.arn` and related actor fields.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Emit probe results from each cloud (success, latency_ms, NXDOMAIN rate) via HEC. Optionally join Route 53 Resolver query logs for SERVFAIL spikes. Page when any critical FQDN fails from two vantage points or latency doubles vs baseline.
Validate ingest before alerting:
```spl
index=cloud sourcetype="dns:health" | stats count by sourcetype
```

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
```spl
index=cloud sourcetype="dns:health" ( OR sourcetype="synthetic:dns")
| table _time userIdentity.arn eventName sourceIPAddress
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.4.23_multi_cloud_dns_resoluti_23"
| sort -_time
```

Understanding this SPL
Scopes `dns:health` in `index=cloud` to detect multi-cloud dns resolution health. Tune thresholds to your change cadence; exclude break-glass principals and sandbox accounts via a lookup.

Step 3 — Validate
Compare to the provider cloud console audit view for the same 24-hour window. Confirm row counts and `userIdentity.arn` values match the vendor console. Run `| fieldsummary` on a 1-hour sample to verify extractions.

Step 4 — Operationalize and troubleshoot
Save as `4_4_23_alert` with severity aligned to `high` criticality. Dashboard: Status grid (FQDN × provider), Line chart (success rate over time), Single value (failed probes)..
Failure modes: (1) no events — verify modular input/API credentials and index routing; (2) empty actor fields — upgrade Custom (synthetic probes, Route 53 Resolver / Azure DNS / Cloud DNS logs) and review alias mappings; (3) API throttling — reduce poll frequency or enable queue buffering; (4) alert fatigue — tune thresholds and document exclusions in knownFalsePositives.
grandmaExplanation: We watch cloud logs for signs of multi-cloud dns resolution health so your team catches problems in your online services before customers or auditors do.
